description: Dangerous-pattern rules for PHP, Ruby, and shell.

rules.title: eval() or assert() on a variable
rules.remediation: Remove it. There is no safe way to eval request-derived data.

rules.title: Shell execution with interpolated input
rules.remediation: Use escapeshellarg() on every interpolated value, or better, avoid the shell and use a purpose-built extension.

rules.title: unserialize() on request data
rules.remediation: PHP object injection leads to code execution through magic methods. Use json_decode instead.

rules.title: include/require with request data
rules.remediation: Map the input to a fixed allowlist of file paths. Remote file inclusion is direct code execution.

rules.title: SQL query containing request data
rules.remediation: Use PDO prepared statements with bound parameters and PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES set to false.

rules.title: Request data echoed without escaping
rules.remediation: Wrap with htmlspecialchars($v, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'), or use a template engine that escapes by default.

rules.title: extract() on request data
rules.remediation: This lets a request overwrite any local variable, including ones used for authorization checks. Read the specific keys you need.

rules.title: preg_replace with the /e modifier
rules.remediation: The /e modifier evaluates the replacement as PHP. Use preg_replace_callback.

rules.title: Weak hash used for a password
rules.remediation: Use password_hash() and password_verify(), which pick a modern algorithm and handle salting for you.

rules.title: Hash compared with a loose operator
rules.remediation: PHP's == coerces types, so a hash beginning '0e' compares equal to any other such hash. Use hash_equals() for constant-time strict comparison.

rules.title: Removed mysql_* extension
rules.remediation: The mysql_* functions were removed in PHP 7 and never supported prepared statements. Migrate to PDO or mysqli.

rules.title: eval with string interpolation
rules.remediation: Replace with a method lookup or a case statement over allowed values.

rules.title: Shell command with interpolation
rules.remediation: Pass arguments as separate values: system('git', 'clone', url). Ruby skips the shell entirely when given multiple arguments.

rules.title: Marshal.load on untrusted data
rules.remediation: Marshal can instantiate arbitrary objects. Use JSON for anything crossing a trust boundary.

rules.title: YAML.load instead of safe_load
rules.remediation: Use YAML.safe_load. On Psych < 4, YAML.load deserializes arbitrary Ruby objects.

rules.title: ActiveRecord query with interpolation
rules.remediation: Use a placeholder form: where('name = ?', name) or where(name: name).

rules.title: html_safe or raw applied to a variable
rules.remediation: html_safe asserts the string is already escaped - it does not escape it. Use sanitize() with an allowlist of tags.

rules.title: Rails CSRF protection skipped
rules.remediation: Only appropriate for token-authenticated API endpoints. If the controller accepts session cookies, this is exploitable.

rules.title: send() with a request-controlled method name
rules.remediation: Lets a request call arbitrary methods. Check the name against an explicit allowlist first.

rules.title: Remote script piped straight into a shell
rules.remediation: Download to a file, verify a checksum or signature, then execute. Piping to a shell executes whatever the server returns, including a partial response.

rules.title: eval on a variable
rules.remediation: Use arrays for argument construction instead of re-parsing a string as a command.

rules.title: TLS verification disabled in a download
rules.remediation: Fix the certificate chain or pass the internal CA with --cacert instead of disabling verification.

rules.title: World-writable permissions
rules.remediation: Grant the narrowest permission that works - 0755 for directories, 0644 for files, 0600 for secrets.

rules.title: Password passed on a command line
rules.remediation: Command lines are visible in `ps` to every user on the host and land in shell history. Use a credentials file with 0600 permissions or an environment variable read from a secret store.

rules.title: rm -rf with an unquoted variable
rules.remediation: If the variable is empty this can delete the wrong tree. Quote it and guard with `[ -n "$VAR" ]` first.

rules.title: Predictable temporary file path
rules.remediation: Use mktemp so the name is unpredictable and created atomically: tmp=$(mktemp).
